title: Pasqal Reports H1 2026 Financial Results: €312.9M Post-SPAC Cash Balance, 14% Revenue Growth, and 1,000-Atom Scale - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Pasqal (NASDAQ: PSQL) reported H1 2026 revenue of €4.87M (+13.7%) with QPU services up 34%, but operating loss tripled to €59.2M on share-based pay and SPAC costs; post-SPAC cash of ~€312.9M on Aug 27 gives substantial runway while it scaled to 1,024 atoms and expanded in Saudi Arabia and Italy.

insights.claim: Pasqal's H1 2026 revenue was €4.87M, up 13.7% from €4.29M in H1 2025, driven by QPU-related services revenue rising 34% to €3.9M.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Revenue remains tiny relative to valuation and losses; QPU services mix is the metric to track.

insights.claim: Pasqal reported €70.4M of booked and awarded business as of June 30, 2026, combining multi-year customer contracts, government grants and tax credits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Backlog is ~14x half-year revenue but includes grants and tax credits, so it is not pure commercial demand.

insights.claim: Pasqal's H1 2026 operating loss widened to €59.16M from €19.77M, including €27.3M of share-based payment charges (vs €1.0M) and €10.2M of one-time listing transaction costs; net loss was €53.24M vs €26.12M.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Stripping SBC and deal costs leaves an underlying operating loss of roughly €21.7M for the half, a better gauge of recurring burn.

insights.claim: Much of Pasqal's tripling operating loss stems from non-cash share-based compensation and one-off SPAC expenses rather than core operating expansion.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Expect headline losses to normalize post-listing, but SBC dilution is a real cost to PSQL shareholders.

insights.claim: Pasqal held €110.8M cash at June 30, 2026, and after closing its SPAC merger with Bleichroeder Acquisition Corp. II and related financing on August 27, 2026, cash rose to about €312.9M ($355.8M).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: At roughly €20-30M of underlying half-year burn, the cash pile implies multi-year runway, reducing near-term dilution risk for PSQL.

insights.claim: Pasqal characterizes its ~€312.9M post-transaction balance as providing substantial runway for ongoing technology execution.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Well-capitalized neutral-atom competitor to listed peers; funding is no longer the binding constraint.
insights.quote: providing substantial runway for ongoing technology execution

insights.claim: Pasqal prepared defect-free registers of 1,024 physical atoms, doubling its prior 506-atom milestone, with a redesigned cryogenic platform extending atom lifetimes about 40-fold.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Keeps Pasqal in the neutral-atom qubit-count race; atom lifetime gains matter for deeper circuits.

insights.claim: Using a photonic integrated circuit co-developed with subsidiary Aeponyx, Pasqal trapped four rubidium atoms with 27.5-second lifetimes while cutting optical footprint by up to 50x, addressing a key neutral-atom scaling constraint.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Chip-based optics could shrink system size and cost; vertical integration via Aeponyx is a differentiator.

insights.claim: Pasqal demonstrated an end-to-end machine-learning application for solving differential equations on logical qubits that outperformed its physical-qubit counterpart.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Early evidence of error-correction payoff on application workloads, a key credibility marker.

insights.claim: Pasqal integrated NVIDIA CUDA-Q into its platform to simplify hybrid quantum-classical workflows across HPC centers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Reinforces NVIDIA's CUDA-Q as a cross-vendor hybrid-quantum standard layer.

insights.claim: Pasqal launched Saudi Arabia's first quantum computer, a 200-qubit QCaaS system, and signed MOUs with Eleven Ventures and KACST to commercialize quantum computing and advance R&D in the kingdom.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gulf sovereign demand is becoming a revenue source for quantum vendors.

insights.claim: Pasqal deployed Italy's first neutral-atom QPU (140 qubits) for integration with the Leonardo supercomputer and advanced capital-markets workflows with Crédit Agricole CIB.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: On-prem HPC-integrated installs are Pasqal's main commercial model in Europe.

insights.claim: Pasqal established a Center of Competency in PIC packaging through Aeponyx at the C2MI facility in Bromont, Quebec, building a Canadian photonic supply chain.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Supply-chain control over photonics is a strategic moat for neutral-atom scaling.

insights.claim: Pasqal is one of five global finalists in the three-year XPRIZE Quantum Applications competition sponsored by Google Quantum AI and GESDA.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Third-party validation of application credibility; a win would be a marketing catalyst.
